title: Fix the Response Aggregator
statement: Read a single line of JSON shaped like {"results": [{"status": "ok"|"error"|"pending", "user": {"id": ..., "score": <stale cached score>, "profile": {"score": <current score>}}}, ...]}. The program below is supposed to walk every entry in `results`, and for entries whose status is exactly "ok" sum up the user's CURRENT score (the one nested under `profile`), counting everything else (including "pending") as an error. It should then print 'ok=<count> error=<count> avg=<average current score of the ok entries, 2 decimal places, or 0.00 if there are no ok entries>'. It has 4 bugs. Fix them so it passes all test cases.
starter_code:
import json

data = json.loads(input())
results = data["results"]

total_score = 0
ok_count = 0
error_count = 0
for entry in results[1:]:
    if entry["status"] == "ok" or entry["status"] == "pending":
        total_score += entry["user"]["score"]
        ok_count += 1
    else:
        error_count += 1

avg = total_score // ok_count if ok_count > 0 else 0
print(f"ok={ok_count} error={error_count} avg={avg:.2f}")
hints: results[1:] silently drops the very first entry from the whole response - is that intended?
"pending" is explicitly called out as NOT ok in the statement - check which statuses the condition actually accepts
Look at the two score fields on `user`: which one is described as the current, authoritative score?
Averaging with // instead of / throws away the decimal part before it's even formatted
